questions.text: What type of learner should take the DevNet Associate course?
options: Anyone that does not like working in teams and is a software developer
Anyone interested in network automation and programmability
questions.explanation: The course is aimed at anyone interested in networking, software development, or the combination of the two: network automation and programmability.

questions.text: What is contained within a DevNet Sandbox?
options: A collection of self-paced tutorials using REST APIs
A collection of Cisco developer API documentation
A preconfigured environment already installed with Cisco platforms
Instructor-led videos focusing on hands-on exercises
questions.explanation: A Sandbox is a pre-configured, production-like test bed with Cisco platforms already installed. Self-paced tutorials are Learning Labs, the API docs are developer documentation, and instructor-led videos are the video courses.

questions.text: Which two DevNet resources are available online? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Code Exchange and Automation Exchange are both online DevNet Exchanges. The DevNet Zone is an in-person area at Cisco Live, and there is no Python Exchange.

questions.text: Which DevNet resource would a developer use if the developer is using a Cisco API and needs help understanding the error message received?
questions.explanation: DevNet Support helps troubleshoot integrations and API connections through tickets, community forums, Webex Teams spaces, and a knowledge base.

options: A vendor-neutral type of virtual networking
A way to create networks using software alone
questions.explanation: DevNet is a developer program: a website, developer community, tools, forums, Learning Labs, and Sandboxes. It isn't a kind of network.

questions.text: What is required in order to ensure that clients are able to talk to applications that are outside a local system?
questions.explanation: Without a network, clients can't reach applications outside the local system. APIs and scripts run over the network; they don't replace it.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the Cisco DevNet Learning Labs?
options: They provide self-paced tutorials including coding.
They allow participants to add their own Python labs.
They allow participants to add their own labs as long as the labs relate to any type of coding.
They provide a space for game development, interaction, and learning based on coding.
questions.explanation: Learning Labs are self-paced tutorials covering coding, REST APIs, model-driven programmability, and Cisco platforms. Participants don't add their own labs.

questions.text: What is a requirement when creating a Cisco DevNet account for accessing educational resources, such as Learning Labs and the DevNet Sandbox?
options: The account must be registered using a Cisco email address.
The account must contain a purchased license.
The account holder must share personally created code before access is allowed.
The account must be created using an existing online identity or via a new Cisco account.
questions.explanation: A DevNet account is free and can be created with an existing online identity or a new Cisco account. No Cisco email, license, or shared code is needed.

questions.text: Which DevNet event is provided by Cisco partners and Cisco offices?
questions.explanation: DevNet Express events are organized by local Cisco partners and Cisco offices. (DevNet Create is a conference, and the DevNet Zone is part of Cisco Live.)

questions.text: Which website provides the entry point for Cisco DevNet?
questions.explanation: developer.cisco.com is the DevNet starting page and the central place for Cisco developer tools and documentation.
